title: Quasi-compact representable stack morphisms on scheme and stack tests
statement: Work with schemes [def-pc-scheme], universes [def-weil-size-convention], algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and the morphisms and $2$-fibre products of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of stack morphisms use [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Let $S$ be a scheme and $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ a morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$, representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]: every scheme base change $h_T:A_T\to T$ has algebraic-space source. Then the following conditions are equivalent: (i) for every scheme $T\to\mathcal B$, the morphism $h_T$ is quasi-compact as a morphism of algebraic spaces; (ii) for every quasi-compact algebraic stack $\mathcal V\to\mathcal B$, the stack $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal V$ is quasi-compact. Thus the representable scheme-test predicate agrees with quasi-compactness as a stack morphism. No separation, finite-type or Deligne--Mumford assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Regard each algebraic space $F$ as its discrete fibred groupoid. A sheaf of sets satisfies stack descent: compatible local sections glue uniquely, and there are only identity arrows to descend. Its representable diagonal has scheme base changes, hence algebraic-space base changes by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. The etale scheme atlas in [def-trf-algebraic-space] is representable, etale and surjective also as a map of fibred groupoids by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]; it is therefore smooth. Thus [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack] makes $F$ an algebraic stack. In particular a scheme is such a stack through its representable sheaf. These are direct applications of the definitions; no existence of an additional atlas is asserted.

source.place: Tag 03YS (lemma-representable-algebraic), (2)-(3), using the defining etale atlas.

proof.text: For an algebraic space $F$, quasi-compactness as a space implies quasi-compactness as a stack: its quasi-compact etale scheme atlas is smooth by the preceding step and is a witness for [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Conversely, a quasi-compact scheme atlas $U\to F$ gives a continuous surjection $|U|\to|F|$ by [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology], whose topology on $F$ agrees with its algebraic-space topology. Its image is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-image-quasi-compact], and the final equivalence in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] supplies a quasi-compact etale scheme atlas. Thus the two quasi-compactness predicates agree. A quasi-compact scheme is a quasi-compact space via the identity etale atlas of [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], and hence a quasi-compact stack. All these implications just substitute the cited atlas definitions and topological equivalence.

Assume (i), and take a quasi-compact algebraic stack $\mathcal V\to\mathcal B$. Choose a smooth surjective atlas $U\to\mathcal V$ with $U$ a quasi-compact scheme, using [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Let $\mathcal W=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal V$; it is algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. Representability of $h$ makes $E=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}U$ an algebraic space, and (i) makes $E\to U$ quasi-compact. Apply the algebraic-space morphism definition in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism] to the quasi-compact space $U\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}U$: $E$ is quasi-compact as a space, hence as a stack by step 2. Reassociation of the defining triples identifies $E$ with $\mathcal W\times_{\mathcal V}U$: it retains the $\mathcal A$-object, the $U$-section and the isomorphism of their images in $\mathcal B$, eliminating the intermediate $\mathcal V$-object using its specified isomorphism to the image of the $U$-section. Thus $E\to\mathcal W$ is a base change of $U\to\mathcal V$, and is smooth and surjective by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. Now [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-quasicompact-surjection] applied to $E\to\mathcal W$ shows that $\mathcal W$ is quasi-compact. This proves (ii).

Assume (ii) and fix a scheme $T\to\mathcal B$. Its base change $E_T=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}T$ is an algebraic space by representability. By the algebraic-space morphism definition in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism], $h_T:E_T\to T$ is quasi-compact when, for every quasi-compact algebraic space $C$ and morphism $C\to T$, the sheaf fibre product $E_T\times_TC$ is quasi-compact. Here the test objects are quasi-compact algebraic spaces, not only schemes, so fix such a $C\to T$. By steps 1 and 2, $C$ is a quasi-compact algebraic stack. Hypothesis (ii) applied to the composite $C\to T\to\mathcal B$ says that the stack $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}C$ is quasi-compact. The defining $2$-fibre-product triples of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] identify it with $E_T\times_TC$. A triple $(a,c,\alpha)$, with $\alpha$ an isomorphism from $h(a)$ to the image of $c$ in $\mathcal B$, goes to $((a,t,\alpha),c)$, where $t$ is the image of $c$ in $T$. Deleting $t$ gives the inverse. Arrows correspond because $T$ and $C$ have only identity arrows. This equivalence over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ carries smooth surjective atlases to smooth surjective atlases. The sheaf $E_T\times_TC$ is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. So step 2 makes it quasi-compact as a space: it has a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme. This is the definition of quasi-compactness of $h_T$, proving (i). Finally (ii) is precisely the stack-morphism quasi-compactness predicate in [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism], so the asserted agreement follows. No step required separation, finite type, or a Deligne--Mumford atlas.

tool_uses.why: Only the final equivalence between compactness of an algebraic-space point set and existence of a quasi-compact etale scheme atlas is used; no moduli or six-functor argument is replaced.
The general topological continuous-image theorem converts the surjective compact scheme atlas to compactness of its point-space target.

Only the first sentence is used: the sheaf fibre product of algebraic spaces is an algebraic space (Stacks 02X2). This is generic algebraic-space infrastructure, given by neither the trace formula nor Poincare duality, and no node of the unit states it.
